items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to requiring motor
vehicle dealer franchisors to fully compensate franchised motor vehicle
dealers for warranty service agreements
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5085

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to requiring
motor vehicle dealer franchisors to fully compensate franchised motor
vehicle dealers for warranty service agreements

 
PURPOSE:

This bill amends the vehicle and traffic law to change the way dealers
are reimbursed by manufacturers; provides that manufacturers must pay a
dealer no less than the amount a retail customer pays the dealer for the
same services; authorizes the use of agreed upon time guides; applies to
warranty work and factory recalls; establishes a manner of determining
effective labor rates.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the vehicle and traffic law to require that all vehicle
franchisors adequately fulfill any warranty agreement, including recalls
and voluntary stop-sell repairs. Warranties will now cover all diagnos-
tic work, as well as ensure adequate compensation for technicians. The
bill would create a time guide to ensure adequate compensation, and
ensures no franchisor shall impose any form of cost recovery fees or
surcharges against a franchised motor vehicle dealer or payments made in
accordance with this proposed legislation.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The licensing and supervision of motor vehicle dealers is necessary for
the protection of consumers. This legislation ensures that the regu-
lation of motor vehicle manufacturers, distributors, wholesalers, facto-
ry branches, distributor branches and representatives will enable
compliance with manufacturer warranties so that consumers can keep their
motor vehicles properly functioning and safe.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to requiring
motor vehicle dealer franchisors to fully compensate franchised motor
vehicle dealers for warranty service agreements

This bill amends the Vehicle and Traffic Law to change the way dealers
are reimbursed by manufacturers; provides that manufacturers must pay a
dealer reasonable compensation for warranty work based off the amount a
retail customer pays the dealer for the same services; applies to
warranty work and factory recalls; establishes a manner of determining
effective labor rates; provides additional guarantees clarifying when
warranty work is covered.

Section 1 amends the Vehicle and Traffic Law to require that all vehicle
franchisors adequately fulfill any warranty agreement, including recalls
and voluntary stop-sell repairs. Warranties will now cover all diagnos-
tic work, as well as ensure adequate compensation for the work
performed. The bill would ensure adequate compensation for all warranty
work, and ensures no franchisor shall reject a vehicle brought in when
warranty work should have been honored due to lack of availability of
parts.

Section 2 contains the effective date

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The licensing and supervision of motor vehicle dealers is necessary for
the protection of consumers. This legislation ensures that the regu-
lation of motor vehicle manufacturers, distributors, wholesalers, facto-
ry branches, distributor branches and representatives will enable
compliance with manufacturer warranties so that consumers can keep their
motor vehicles properly functioning and safe.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

None

C.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5085C

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to requiring
motor vehicle dealer franchisors to fully compensate franchised motor
vehicle dealers for warranty service agreements

 
PURPOSE:

This bill amends the Vehicle and Traffic Law to change the way dealers
are reimbursed by manufacturers; provides that manufacturers must pay a
dealer reasonable compensation for warranty work based off the amount a
retail customer pays the dealer for the same services; applies to
warranty work and factory recalls; establishes a manner of determining
effective labor rates; provides additional guarantees clarifying when
warranty work is covered.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the Vehicle and Traffic Law to require that all vehicle
franchisors adequately fulfill any warranty agreement, including
recalls, voluntary stop-sell repairs, extended warranties, and similar
items. Warranties will now cover all diagnostic work, as well as ensure
adequate reasonable compensation for the work performed. The bill would
ensure adequate reasonable compensation for all warranty work and
ensures no franchisor shall reject a vehicle brought in when warranty
work should have been honored due to lack of availability of parts.

Section 2 contains the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The licensing and supervision of motor vehicle dealers is necessary for
the protection of consumers. This legislation ensures that the regu-
lation of motor vehicle manufacturers, distributors, wholesalers, facto-
ry branches, distributor branches and representatives will enable
compliance with manufacturer warranties so that consumers can keep their
motor vehicles properly functioning and safe.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
